rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong multimodal baseline using the most expressive components to set a high performance bar and reduce uncertainty about whether the full multimodal pipeline is viable. config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) combines a pretrained RNA foundation model (scgpt), the strongest image encoder (ViT-L), the most expressive aggregation (transformer), and a flexible learned fusion (weighted). If this configuration performs well, it confirms the multimodal direction and gives me a strong anchor to ablate specific components in subsequent experiments. If it underperforms, it signals that one or more of these choices is suboptimal, directing me toward simpler or alternative encoders/aggregations. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the tight 10-experiment budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_037: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation + weighted fusion, acc≈0.52), the most important uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation layer is actually contributing meaningful performance over a simpler alternative. Config_016 is identical to config_037 except it replaces transformer aggregation with avgpool, isolating that single architectural variable. If avgpool performs comparably, it tells us the transformer is not a critical component and we can redirect remaining budget toward other dimensions (encoder choice, fusion, profile setting). If transformer is clearly superior, it confirms the current architectural direction and we should exploit it further. This minimal single-variable change from the current best is the highest-information experiment we can run with 8 trials remaining, as it directly tests a fundamental design choice without conflating multiple factors.

Evidence: Both completed experiments (config_037, config_016) share scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion + multiprofile, differing only in aggregation (transformer=0.520 vs avgpool=0.542), suggesting avgpool is preferable. However, we have zero information about whether the RNA encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) materially affects performance. Question: config_045 keeps all best-known settings (avgpool, weighted, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile) and swaps scgpt for scvi_n200, isolating the RNA encoder as the single variable. Why this is the best next step: The RNA encoder is the most impactful untested dimension—it determines the quality of the single-cell representation before fusion. With 7 experiments remaining, resolving whether a learned VAE (scvi_n200) can match or beat the generative pre-trained scgpt will either open a new promising branch or confirm scgpt as the anchor, allowing subsequent experiments to focus on image encoder, fusion, and profile-setting choices with higher confidence.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 as RNA encoder dramatically outperforms scgpt (0.706 vs ~0.52-0.54) with the same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted). The current best (config_045) uses imagenet_vit_l, but we have no data on how the image encoder interacts with scvi_n200. config_007 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the cleanest single-variable test: it changes only the image encoder from the current best, isolating whether resnet50 provides complementary or superior visual features when paired with the scvi_n200 RNA representation. This is the highest-impact untested dimension (image encoder is more fundamental than aggregation, which showed only ~2% difference with scgpt), and resolving it early with 6 experiments remaining will guide the rest of the search toward the best image-RNA pairing.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the superior RNA encoder (0.706/0.678 vs 0.520/0.542 for scgpt), and imagenet_vit_l outperforms resnet50 with scvi_n200 (0.706 vs 0.678). The best config (config_045) uses avgpool+weighted. However, the avgpool>transformer finding was only observed with the weaker scgpt encoder; with scvi_n200's richer latent representations, transformer aggregation may better capture cross-modal interactions. This experiment (config_043: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable change from the current best, testing whether transformer aggregation can push accuracy above 0.706 while keeping the proven fusion strategy. With 5 experiments remaining, exploiting the clearly dominant scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l direction while resolving the aggregation question is the highest-value next step.

Evidence: The top-5 experiments clearly show scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l is the dominant combination (0.706–0.725 acc), with transformer aggregation slightly outperforming avgpool (config_043: 0.725 vs config_045: 0.706). All top performers use weighted fusion. Uncertainty: Whether concat fusion could outperform weighted fusion for this best-known encoder/aggregation pairing remains untested. This experiment (config_047: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat, multiprofile) isolates the fusion strategy as the single variable changed from the current best (config_043). Rationale: With 4 experiments left, exploiting the strongest direction with a minimal, targeted change is the highest-information-use move. If concat matches or beats weighted, we gain a new best; if not, we confirm weighted is optimal and can focus remaining budget on other axes (e.g., profile setting or alternative encoders).

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l is clearly the best encoder pair (0.706–0.725 vs 0.52–0.68 for others), and transformer aggregation + weighted fusion (config_043, 0.725) is the current best. We have tested 3 of 4 aggregation×fusion combinations for this pair (avgpool+weighted=0.706, transformer+weighted=0.725, transformer+concat=0.721). Question: config_013 (avgpool+concat) completes the 2×2 matrix, clarifying whether the small weighted-over-concat gap (~0.4%) is consistent across aggregation types and whether we have truly reached the ceiling for this encoder pair. Why best use of budget: With only 3 experiments remaining, confirming whether 0.725 is the practical optimum for the best-encoder combination lets us decide whether to exploit further (unlikely to gain much) or pivot to a different architectural direction. It is the lowest-risk, highest-information experiment that directly constrains the search space.

Evidence: The top 4 experiments all use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, with transformer+weighted (config_043, 0.725) as the best. We've fully explored that 2x2 aggregation×fusion space. The only untested scvi_n200 multimodal direction is with resnet50 (only avgpool+weighted was tested at 0.678). Question: Does transformer aggregation provide the same ~1-2% boost with resnet50 that it did with ViT? This tests whether the aggregation benefit is encoder-agnostic or specific to ViT's patch structure. Why this is the best use: With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the most logical exploitation step — it extends our strongest evidence (scvi_n200 + transformer + weighted) to the one untested image encoder, clarifying whether the architecture is robust or whether ViT is essential. If it approaches 0.70+, it confirms we're near the ceiling for this model family; if it lags significantly, it reinforces that imagenet_vit_l is critical and we should accept config_043 as the likely optimum.

The current best is config_043 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy. All four aggregation×fusion combinations for scvi_n200+imagenet_vit_l are exhausted, leaving only resnet50 variants untested in the top-performing encoder family. config_018 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved the highest F1 of all experiments (0.6945), suggesting the resnet50+transformer pairing captures complementary discriminative signal. config_023 tests whether concat fusion with this pairing can approach or exceed the weighted-fusion result, completing the scvi_n200 multimodal multiprofile grid. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, selecting the most informative untested configuration in the proven top-performing encoder space (scvi_n200) maximizes the chance of either finding a new best or confirming the ceiling of this architecture family.

The current best (config_043: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, acc=0.725) has exhausted all scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l multimodal multiprofile combinations. The remaining major uncertainty is whether the RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs. alternatives) is the dominant factor or whether the architecture (transformer + weighted + ViT-L) is what drives performance. config_046 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) isolates the RNA encoder variable by swapping scvi_n200 for pca_n2000 while keeping the exact best architecture. While scgpt underperformed scvi_n200 by ~0.2, PCA at 2000 dimensions is a fundamentally different (linear, high-dimensional) representation that could capture complementary variance. As the final experiment, this is the highest-information test: if PCA approaches 0.725, it reveals the architecture is the key driver; if it falls well short, it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and solidifies config_043 as the definitive best. No other untested config has a plausible path to exceeding 0.725.
